description: We are Ga Tidur, a team of Indonesian Informatics students passionate about AI, machine learning, Earth observation, and environmental research. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire detections to better understand historical fire activity. Our goal is to build an interactive, evidence-based platform that makes satellite data more accessible and supports environmental awareness, scientific analysis, and future humanitarian applications.
summary:
VESTIGIUM is an evidence-led historical satellite fire intelligence platform developed by Team Ga Tidur for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Addressing the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge, VESTIGIUM transforms NASA FIRMS satellite observations from Indonesia (2000–2025) into an interactive historical atlas.

The project combines data engineering, geospatial analysis, and experimental machine learning to harmonize MODIS detection counts with the VIIRS S-NPP observation scale.

Through interactive maps, historical timelines, and analytical visualizations, users can explore thermal anomaly patterns, investigate historical changes, and understand the limitations of satellite observations.

VESTIGIUM emphasizes scientific transparency: satellite hotspots are thermal detections, not confirmed individual fires or evidence of their causes.

Our mission is to make historical environmental data more accessible, interpretable, and useful for scientific research, environmental monitoring, and public accountability.
details:
VESTIGIUM: Earth Remembers What Fire Leaves Behind

Project Overview

VESTIGIUM is an evidence-led historical satellite fire intelligence platform developed by Team Ga Tidur. It addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" by making satellite thermal anomaly observations more accessible, comparable, and scientifically interpretable.

How It Works

The project analyzes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS observations across Indonesia from 2000 to 2025.

Our research pipeline includes:

  1. Data Engineering: Cleaning, validating, and organizing satellite observations while preserving sensor identity and data provenance.
  2. Geospatial Processing: Aggregating observations into 25-km equal-area grid cells using EPSG:6933.
  3. Sensor Harmonization: Experimentally calibrating MODIS thermal-pixel detection counts to approximate the VIIRS S-NPP detection-count scale using Poisson gradient boosting.
  4. Interactive Visualization: Providing an investigative web atlas with geographic exploration, temporal analysis, satellite filtering, and observation metadata.

Scientific Evaluation

The archived analysis contains 5,997,676 accepted thermal-pixel detection records.

In the historical 2023–2025 temporal holdout, the experimental Poisson boosting model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 10.24, compared with 15.67 for uncalibrated MODIS counts.

However, the model does not outperform every baseline on RMSE and cannot reconstruct missing VIIRS detections or identify individual wildfire events.

These evaluation results originate from an earlier full-dataset experiment. The restructured repository pipeline has been tested using synthetic fixtures but has not yet been independently rerun against the complete original dataset.

User Experience

Users can explore historical thermal detections, filter observations by time and satellite, inspect evidence metadata, and analyze temporal patterns.

The application clearly distinguishes actual data from synthetic demonstration records. When production data artifacts are unavailable, the interface displays labeled synthetic demo observations.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, MapLibre GL JS
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Data processing: Python, SQLite, geospatial processing
  • Machine learning: Scikit-learn, Poisson gradient boosting
  • Data source: NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS

Innovation and Impact

VESTIGIUM combines experimental satellite sensor harmonization with transparent visual investigation and explicit scientific limitations.

Rather than treating satellite detections as confirmed wildfires or evidence of intentional burning, the project emphasizes reproducibility, uncertainty, and responsible environmental interpretation.

Its long-term purpose is to support scientific investigation, historical environmental research, and public accountability.

Future Development

Future work includes deploying verified production datasets, accounting for satellite observation opportunities and cloud coverage, performing spatially independent validation, and integrating independently verified burned-area and land-cover observations.

AI Assistance Disclosure

Generative AI tools assisted with software development, documentation, content drafting, and presentation design. Scientific observations are attributed to NASA FIRMS. Synthetic demonstration observations are explicitly labeled and are not presented as real satellite measurements.

VESTIGIUM is an independent participant project, not an official NASA product.
